prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Weekly On-Call Rotation Schedule (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "Week 14(Mar 30 – Apr 5)" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Week 15(Apr 6 – 12)" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Week 16(Apr 13 – 19)" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Week" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 105px
  col 2: header "Role" · longest unbreakable word 68px · one-line width 68px
  col 3: header "Engineer" · longest unbreakable word 80px · one-line width 114px
  col 4: header "Phone" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 116px
  col 5: header "Escalation notes" · longest unbreakable word 79px · one-line width 579px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 645px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 644px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Show who is on call each week, how to reach them, and what escalation or coverage conditions apply.","reading":"Readers find a week, scan its primary and secondary rows, then match each engineer and phone number to the relevant notes. The merged week cells already span two rows, so wrapped week labels can use that shared height.","groups":["Week and Role establish the schedule and distinguish the two assignments within each week.","Engineer and Phone form a contact pair that readers need to match quickly.","Escalation notes provide instructions and exceptions for each assignment."],"keep_intact":["Primary and Secondary role labels","Phone numbers, for reliable reading and dialing","Individual name components and date ranges where space permits"],"may_wrap":["Week labels between the week number and date range","Engineer names between given and family names","Escalation notes at natural word boundaries"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [110, 89, 101, 137, 207] · table 645×515px · row heights [33, 73, 73, 94, 73, 73, 94] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2B: widths [85, 89, 101, 137, 232] · table 645×455px · row heights [33, 73, 53, 73, 73, 73, 73] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r2C: widths [100, 89, 101, 137, 217] · table 645×495px · row heights [33, 73, 73, 73, 73, 73, 94] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
